ledger.note: 184: the Liang Province rebellion begins. 'The rebellion began in the winter of 184' with two Qiang groups, and escalated in 'October or November 184' when Auxiliary troops mutinied at Lianju; the rebels took Qianya and made Jincheng 'their main stronghold'.

region.text: Meiyang (west of Wugong) and Chencang, where Han armies met the rebels in 185 and 188-189

ledger.note: 185: the Han armies meet the rebels west of Chang'an. Zhang Wen, appointed in the eighth lunar month of 185, camped at Meiyang (west of Wugong); in the eleventh month Dong Zhuo 'smashed the rebel army in a sudden attack'.

region.text: 'the entire Liang Province', held by the rebels from 187

ledger.note: 187: the whole province. In 187 the rebels 'extended their sway over the entire Liang Province' for the first time; Han Sui took Longxi after its Grand Administrator defected, and Hanyang was besieged after the Didao mutiny.

region.text: Meiyang (west of Wugong) and Chencang, where Han armies met the rebels in 185 and 188-189

ledger.note: 189: the siege of Chencang fails. 'Wang Guo's men laid siege to Chencang for more than eighty days with no success'; 'In spring 189, Wang Guo's men became worn out and abandoned the siege', Huangfu Song pursuing.

region.text: 'the entire Liang Province', held by the rebels from 187

ledger.note: 189: the rebellion splits. After Emperor Ling's death on 13 May 189 the Liang rebellion 'became subsumed as an outlying disturbance' and 'finally splintered into three groups: Han Sui's group in Jincheng, Ma Teng's group in the Wei Valley, Song Jian's group in Fuhan'.

wars.outcome: The rebels held Jincheng from 184 and the whole province from 187; Han armies beat them at Meiyang in 185 and Wang Guo failed at Chencang in 189; the rebellion passed into the warlordism of Han Sui, Ma Teng and Song Jian.
wars.note: The Huangfu Song and Zhang Wen commands (185) and Dong Zhuo's victory in the eleventh month of 185 are on the page.

certainty.note: The page names commanderies and the province, never a frontier.

sources.title: Liang Province rebellion
sources.note: The 184-189 rebellion: Jincheng, 187 sway over the entire province, Meiyang 185, Chencang 188-189, the three groups of 189, Song Jian to 214.

sources.title: Han Sui
sources.note: Co-ruler of Liang Province with Ma Teng; 192 submission and Chang'an defeat; 200 peace; died June or July 215.

sources.title: Ma Teng
sources.note: Controlled Liang Province with Han Sui; summoned to Ye 208; executed June or July 212; Tong Pass September 211.

sources.title: End of the Han dynasty
sources.note: Ma Teng and Han Sui "controlled Yong and Liang provinces" (197); defeated at Tong Pass 211.

notes:
Liang Province rebels, 184-189 (rebel). 1 page used for events (Liang Province rebellion) plus the Han Sui and Ma Teng pages for the succession. No Cliopatria row; the Han shape keeps Liang Province throughout.
Unsettled: (1) 'winter of 184' against 'October or November 184' (no month entered); (2) the page does not say when Longxi and Hanyang were taken, only that they were besieged or defected by 187; (3) the page says only that after Emperor Ling's death on 13 May 189 the rebellion 'finally splintered' by year's end, so the dissolve has no month; (4) Qiang and Lesser Yuezhi participants are not given a territory of their own.
Counterparts: han-dynasty exists; han-sui and song-jian are written by this batch.
